question.problem: Given that $10{x}^{6}+29{x}^{3}-21=(a{x}^{3}-3)(2{x}^{3}+b)$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers, find the value of $a+b.$
question.worked_solution:
We can introduce a new variable $z={x}^{3}$ and then rewrite the trinomial as a quadratic in terms of $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}10{x}^{6}+29{x}^{3}-21 & =10{({x}^{3})}^{2}+29({x}^{3})-21 \\  & =10{z}^{2}+29z-21\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the quadratic, and then rewrite the final expression in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}10{z}^{2}+29z-21 & =(5z-3)(2z+7) \\  & =(5{x}^{3}-3)(2{x}^{3}+7)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $a=5$, $b=7$ and $a+b=12.$
